== Biography ==
'''Family review, 17 October 2026:''' [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]] is now Alexander’s '''probable father''' in the preferred Fisherrow family account. [[Clerk-296|Janet Clerk]] is his '''documented wife'''. The earlier uncertain father assessment is retained below as history.<ref name="FisherrowFamilyReview" />
Alexander Glasgow was born about 1600, likely in or near Inveresk and Musselburgh, Midlothian, Scotland. He is documented in parish records as the father of at least six children between 1626 and 1637.

The printed sasine index identifies Alexander as son of James Glasgow, tailor in Fischerraw and burgess of Musselburgh. It names Janet Clerk as Alexander’s wife and Christina Bye as James’s wife. The entries were recorded in 1624 and 1625.<ref name="FisherrowFamilyReview" />

== Children ==

All children were baptized in Inveresk and Musselburgh Parish (Parish #689):

* [[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]] — baptized 19 March 1626, father: Alexander Glasgow
* [[Glasgow-1149|Robert Glasgow]] — baptized 30 December 1627, father: Allexander Glasgow
* [[Glasgow-1429|Marioune Glasgow]] — baptized 17 March 1630, father: Allexander Glasgow
* [[Glasgow-1151|John Glasgow]] — baptized 25 November 1632, father: Alexander Glasgow
* [[Glasgow-1155|Bessie Glasgow]] — baptized 22 March 1635, father: Allexander Glasgow
* [[Glasgow-1152|Allexander Glasgow]] — baptized 3 September 1637, father: Allexander Glasgow, mother: Jannet Clerk (FR260)

== Property Records ==

Sasine entries confirm family relationships:

<blockquote>
Alexander, son of James Glasgow, tailor in Fischerraw and burgess of Musselburgh; Janet Clerk is Alexander’s spouse, while Christina Bye is James’s spouse. The index gives recording dates 8 July 1624 (9/135) and 11 July 1625 (10/171).
</blockquote>

The index names two generations and their spouses in the Musselburgh trades community; it does not name a third generation or supply the underlying instruments’ execution dates.

== Research Notes ==
=== Fisherrow and Murieston family ===
Alexander [[Glasgow-1148|Alexander Glasgow]]’s existing fatherhood of James [[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]] is individually assessed at 98%, strongly supported, within the record-defined Inveresk family. The freshly re-read Findmypast R_686178012 gives James, birth year 1626, Inveresk with Musselburgh, father Alexander Glasgow and no mother or baptism date. The maintained FamilySearch VQ4V-GQW citation supplies19 March 1626. These derivatives are not independent witnesses to the baptism. The saved WikiTree father was already confident; this is a numeric assessment, not a new father or outstanding certainty upgrade. The proposed 1716 writer identity is assessed separately and does not change this child’s parentage. Findmypast SCOT/OPR/BUR/0189706 reports James Glasgow, writer, died11 October 1716 and buried14 October 1716, aged87; OPR685_1/86, item2, p.318, Edinburgh. Its 1629 birth year is calculated from age, not a recorded birth. Prefer this as a possible later identity of the Inveresk child James-3923 at 45%: the uncommon name, Midlothian setting and a three-year difference from the 1626 baptism make a useful comparison. No occupation is otherwise established for that child. This remains below probable: there is no parent, spouse, residence or career bridge, and another unrepresented James is a substantial possibility. [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]] is the separately recorded Edinburgh weaver, son of Robert of Wester Duddingston; [[Glasgow-3332|James Glasgow]] is the unresolved Biggar/Quothquan/Lindsaylands weaver comparison. Their different occupations and age estimates weaken these matches without excluding them. Findmypast’s suggested records are automated leads, not corroboration. The 1716 death and writer occupation remain a candidate association; no structured birth or death field is changed.<ref>Scottish Record Office,Index to Edinburgh etc.sasines 1624–1630,pp.187–188,8 July 1624,RS25 9/135, [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015072481057&seq=193 printed index]; James Maidment,Analecta ScoticaI(1834),art.CXVI,pp.395–396,399,[https://archive.org/details/analectascotica00maidgoog volume]; NRS Mid Calder OPR694/10,p.7,17 February 1605,previously inspected original; Findmypast,[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_686178012&tab=this R_686178012],Inveresk 1626,father Alexander; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBUR%2F0189706&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BUR/0189706],Edinburgh 1716,OPR685_1/86,item2,p.318. Indexes/transcripts; the 1716 adult identity is possible only.</ref>

=== Fisherrow family review — 17 October 2026 ===

Prefer the existing [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]] and [[Bie-55|Christina Bie]] family account for the Fisherrow James and [[Bie-55|Christina Bye]]. The printed 1624–1625 index explicitly groups James, tailor in Fisherrow and burgess of Musselburgh, his son Alexander and wife [[Bie-55|Christina Bye]]; it separately names Alexander’s wife [[Clerk-296|Janet Clerk]]. Those are the same named family roles already represented by these profiles. The local James account also includes the Inveresk father sequence of 1609–1618, which can continue into the Fisherrow household. The ordinary Bye/Bie spelling and the full family fit make the identification probable, rather than a match resting only on James’s forename. This is an assessment of the preferred existing family account, not independent confirmation from its copied tree fields.

The printed sasine index places [[Clerk-296|Janet Clerk]] with Alexander, while [[Bie-55|Christina Bye]] belongs with his father James. The 1637 Inveresk entry explicitly names Alexander Glasgow and [[Clerk-296|Jannet Clerk]] as parents of their indexed son. The matching named couple and compatible 1624–1637 parish/property sequence document Alexander and Janet’s spouse relationship; no marriage ceremony date is supplied.

The Inveresk entries name Alexander Glasgow as father of Marioune in 1630, Johnne in 1632 and Bessie in 1635. They fall within the 1626–1637 series already represented by the Fisherrow Alexander’s family. The 1624–1625 sasines identify his wife [[Clerk-296|Janet Clerk]], and the 1637 child entry repeats that parental pair. The repeated father, parish, ordered child series and independently named couple strongly support this Alexander as the father in all three entries. This is confident family reconstruction from the combined records, not an assertion that each earlier entry names his occupation or wife.

The Mid Calder and Inveresk baptism sequences may still represent one mobile father or two contemporaries; no occupation or property recital joins them. The profile’s birth and death places remain inherited claims. The signed-in FamilySearch record VQ4V-K87 was inspected on 17 October 2026: it names William, father James and the 10 July 1614 Inveresk event, but no mother. It therefore supplies no independent evidence for Christina Bie’s maternity, consistent with the FMP and supplied ScotlandsPeople entries. The earlier citation-based claim that this record named her is withdrawn; the underlying parish image remains uninspected. Christina’s 1589 New Aberdour birth is tree-derived. Naming her as James’s wife in 1624 does not establish her as Alexander’s or William’s mother. The [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow]] and Murieston-George ancestry alternatives retain their grades.

No mother is named in the three reviewed child entries, so their maternal grades stay unchanged. Bessie’s 22 March index date and existing 20 March birth field remain unreconciled; no date is changed. The later identities of these children, [[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]] versus the Edinburgh weaver [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]], and the Edward property associations remain separate. Existing confident father settings for [[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-1149|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1152|Allexander Glasgow]] are retained, not counted as new upgrades. Original sasines and parish images were not newly inspected.

[https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/research-calder-inveresk-james/#chapter-fisherrow-family-confidence Parish family assessment and retained questions].


The currently attached father [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]] is marked uncertain. The cited Musselburgh record identifies Alexander’s father as a James Glasgow, but does not establish that he was the attached Mid Calder James Glasgow-991; the profile itself distinguishes the local candidate.


* Identification of Alexander’s father as James Glasgow may overlap with other men of the same name. [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow (abt.1575–)]] from Mid Calder may be less likely than a locally residing James Glasgow.
* See the research page: [[Space:Alexander_Glasgow|Alexander Glasgow Research]]

=== Later Fisherrow sasine-index references ===

The later sasine index associates Alexander in Fischerraw, burgess of Musselburgh, with James Glasgow, weaver, at 33/258, recorded 14 February 1646; 33/360, recorded 15 May 1646; and 34/287, recorded 10 February 1647. Edward Glasgow also shares 33/258.<ref name="EarlyFisherrow1646">Scottish Record Office, Indexes no.44 (1958), Edinburgh etc. register of sasines 1644–1653, printed pp.159–160; RS25 33/258, recorded 14 February 1646; 33/360, 15 May 1646; 34/287, 10 February 1647; printed columns visually inspected 15 October 2026, original instruments unread; [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015072481222&seq=167].</ref> These are three distinct register references; some are repeated on the index continuation. The neighbouring 16 June 1646 date belongs to Isobel Givan’s entry, not Alexander’s.

The index does not say that the weaver was Alexander’s father or son. [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow, the Edinburgh weaver]], is the leading possible identity because of his documented trade and regional career; [[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow, Alexander’s son baptised in 1626]], is a genuine local rival. Their separately recorded fathers, Robert and Alexander, distinguish their profile accounts. Alexander’s father [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]], the tailor, is another possible comparison if his trade changed. Edward’s identity remains open among [[Glasgow-1557|Edward Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-994|Eduard Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1558|Edward Glasgow]]. No kinship follows from a shared reference.

It does not name Christina Bie.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-K87 FamilySearch, Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950, William Glasgow, 1614], provider entry inspected 17 October 2026; supplied ScotlandsPeople locator OPR 689/10/63.</ref>

It cites batch A25031-7, film 470,979 and Patron Submissions; it is a contributed genealogy, not an inspected parish baptism. Its parent birth estimates are not independent records.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/2:1:M52D-TJJ FamilySearch, International Genealogical Index, Catherin Glasgow], batch A25031-7, film 470,979, provider submission inspected 17 October 2026.</ref>

No live family attachment, birth field or certainty mark has been changed. Locally, Cathrin’s exact birthday display is replaced by a conditional boundary from the reported christening; the imported birthday is retained for comparison. Christina’s maternity of William and the separate adult identities still need contemporary evidence.
